# MCP reference

28 tools at `/mcp` (streamable HTTP, `Authorization: Bearer <token>`) or over stdio (`slate-mcp` with `SLATE_URL` and `SLATE_TOKEN`). Each tool takes `{"action": ..., "params": {...}}` (single-action tools take only `params`) and an optional `session_ref` recorded on every event it writes. Null fields are dropped from results. Setup: [../mcp.md](../mcp.md).

`*` marks a required param. **REST** is the call the action makes in stdio mode and the route that does the same over HTTP.

## `slate_item`

Read and change items (tasks) on Slate, the workspace's task board: find, file, update, move, assign, tag, comment, report what you are doing (live badge), archive, split and read history. Use it whenever you file, look up or progress a piece of work.

| Action | Scope | Params | REST | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `get` | `read` | `id`\* | `GET /items/{item_id}` | the item with subtasks, comments and last 20 events |
| `list` | `read` | `list_id`, `section_id`, `status`, `assignee`, `tag`, `external_ref`, `due_before`, `due_after`, `q`, `stale`, `include_archived`, `archived`, `trashed`, `closed`, `order`, `kind`, `blocked`, `changed_since`, `fields`, `limit`, `offset`, `ids`, `open_comment_for` | `GET /items` | items matching every filter given (AND); `fields` trims each item, `changed_since` returns only items changed after an event id, `limit`/`offset` page |
| `create` | `write` | `body_md`, `body_note`, `status`, `priority`, `start_at`, `due_at`, `waiting_on_account_id`, `acceptance_md`, `position`, `kind`, `external_ref`, `assignees`, `tags`, `estimate_minutes`, `title`\*, `list_id`, `parent_id` | `POST /items` | file ONE item in list_id (parent_id instead makes it one subtask) |
| `update` | `write` | `body_md`, `body_note`, `status`, `priority`, `start_at`, `due_at`, `waiting_on_account_id`, `acceptance_md`, `position`, `kind`, `external_ref`, `assignees`, `tags`, `estimate_minutes`, `title`, `id`\* | `PATCH /items/{item_id}` | change any fields; null clears; assignees/tags replace the set |
| `set_status` | `write` | `id`\*, `status`\* | `PATCH /items/{item_id}` | move to a status of its list (done stamps completed_at) |
| `assign` | `write` | `id`\*, `assignees`\* | `PATCH /items/{item_id}` | set who it is assigned to (replaces the set; to take an item yourself, `report` with assign_me) |
| `tag` | `write` | `id`\*, `tags`\* | `PATCH /items/{item_id}` | set its tags |
| `report` | `write` | `run_id`, `state`\*, `note`, `progress`, `comment`, `complete`, `waiting_on`, `assign_me`, `url`, `claim`, `reply`, `thread`, `id`\* | `POST /items/{item_id}/report` | say what you are doing on it: state working / blocked / review shows a live badge on the card (with note and progress); done clears it and completes the item; idle clears it. The note is also posted as your comment |
| `run` | `write` | `id`\* | `POST /items/{item_id}/run` | Run now: ask the item's agent assignees to start on it now (records item.run_requested; their runners take it at once). Refused when no agent is assigned or it is done, cancelled or archived |
| `brief` | `read` | `ask`, `id`\* | `GET /items/{item_id}/brief` | the task as one paste-ready prompt (title, due, description, checklists, recent comments) ending with the run rule: finish with a last line `SLATE: done`, `SLATE: review`, `SLATE: later` or `SLATE: blocked waiting_on <handle>`; a comment ending so reports back |
| `comment` | `write` | `id`\*, `body_md`\* | `POST /items/{item_id}/comments` | add a comment |
| `bulk_update` | `write` | `ids`\*, `changes`\* | `POST /items/bulk` | apply one change to many items at once (all or nothing; up to 500) |
| `archive` | `write` | `id`\* | `POST /items/{item_id}/archive` | hide it and its subtasks (soft; history stays) |
| `unarchive` | `write` | `id`\* | `POST /items/{item_id}/unarchive` | bring it back |
| `trash` | `write` | `id`\* | `POST /items/{item_id}/trash` | move it (and its subtasks) to the trash: hidden, restorable, deleted for good after the trash period (30 days by default) |
| `restore` | `write` | `id`\* | `POST /items/{item_id}/restore` | take it out of the trash |
| `purge` | `write` | `id`\* | `POST /items/{item_id}/purge` | delete a trashed item for good (history stays) |
| `split` | `write` | `children`\*, `id`\* | `POST /items/{item_id}/split` | create several subtasks under it: the only multi-child path |
| `delete` | `write` | `id`\* | `DELETE /items/{item_id}` | undo your own create within 10 minutes; otherwise archive |
| `link` | `write` | `kind`\*, `item_id`\*, `id`\* | `POST /items/{item_id}/links` | add a link: kind blocks / blocked_by / relates / duplicate_of / duplicated_by, from this item's side |
| `unlink` | `write` | `kind`\*, `item_id`\*, `id`\* | `DELETE /items/{item_id}/links` | remove a dependency (same kind and item_id as when added) |
| `activity` | `read` | `include`, `limit`, `id`\* | `GET /items/{item_id}/activity` | comments and history in one list, oldest first (what people see beside the task) |
| `watch` | `write` | `account`, `id`\* | `POST /items/{item_id}/watch` | add a watcher (you, or `account`): watchers hear about every change to the item (check-in `watching`, inbox, an assignee_me webhook) |
| `unwatch` | `write` | `account`, `id`\* | `POST /items/{item_id}/unwatch` | remove a watcher (you, or `account`) |
| `watchers` | `read` | `id`\* | `GET /items/{item_id}/watchers` | who follows the item |
| `set_watchers` | `write` | `watchers`\*, `id`\* | `PUT /items/{item_id}/watchers` | replace who follows the item (handles or ids) |
| `attachments` | `read` | `id`\* | `GET /items/{item_id}/attachments` | the item's files: id, filename, size, content type |
| `detach` | `write` | `id`\* | `DELETE /attachments/{attachment_id}` | remove one attachment by its id |
| `attach` | `write` | `filename`\*, `content_base64`\*, `content_type`, `id`\* | `POST /items/{item_id}/attachments/base64` | attach a file (base64) to the item |
| `promote_attachment` | `write` | `title`, `parent_id`, `list_id`, `section_id`, `note`, `id`\* | `POST /attachments/{attachment_id}/promote` | move an attachment into Docs & Files: a file doc with the bytes as revision 1; the task gets a comment linking it |
| `history` | `read` | `id`\* | `GET /items/{item_id}/events` | every event on the item, oldest first |
| `versions` | `read` | `id`\* | `GET /items/{item_id}/versions` | every body version, oldest first |
| `revert` | `write` | `event_id`\* | `POST /events/{event_id}/revert` | undo one change from the history (an item.updated field, item.status_changed, item.assigned or item.moved event) by issuing its inverse as you: a new event, session_ref revert:<event_id>. Refused when the field has changed again since |

## `slate_comment`

Comments are the conversation on an item; @handle mentions an account and reaches its inbox and assignee_me webhook. Use it to ask someone something, answer, or react; for progress on work you hold, slate_item report shows it on the card.

| Action | Scope | Params | REST | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `list` | `read` | `id`\* | `GET /items/{item_id}/comments` | the item's comments, oldest first, with reactions |
| `add` | `write` | `body_md`\*, `assignee`, `keep_open`, `id`\* | `POST /items/{item_id}/comments` | comment on item id; @handle mentions an account; assignee makes it an Ask (open in their queue until explicitly resolved); replies notify earlier participants but do not resolve Asks; keep_open is accepted for compatibility |
| `assign` | `write` | `id`\*, `assignee`\* | `PATCH /comments/{comment_id}` | address a comment to an account, or take it off with assignee null (id is the comment id; the author or an admin) |
| `resolve` | `write` | `id`\* | `POST /comments/{comment_id}/resolve` | close an Ask (id is the comment id; its assignee, author or an admin) |
| `edit` | `write` | `id`\*, `body_md`\* | `PATCH /comments/{comment_id}` | edit your own comment (id is the comment id) |
| `delete` | `write` | `id`\* | `DELETE /comments/{comment_id}` | delete a comment for good (id is the comment id; your own, or anyone's as an admin) |
| `react` | `write` | `emoji`\*, `id`\* | `POST /comments/{comment_id}/reactions` | add your emoji reaction to a comment |
| `unreact` | `write` | `emoji`\*, `id`\* | `DELETE /comments/{comment_id}/reactions/{emoji}` | remove your emoji reaction |

## `slate_chat`

Chat channels: General, one per section, one per list and one per agent (channel `general`, `list:<id>`, `section:<id>`, `agent:<id>`), with threads, reactions and @mentions. Use it to talk with people and other agents about a list's work, answer a mention or thread reply from check-in, or turn a message into a task. Your own chat (`agent:<your id>`) is where a person talks to you outside any card: every message they post there mentions you; answer there. A message's `files` are what was sent with it (a screenshot, a PDF): read one with GET /api/v1/message-files/<id>.

| Action | Scope | Params | REST | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `channels` | `read` | — | `GET /channels` | every channel in board order with your unread and mention counts |
| `messages` | `read` | `before`, `after`, `limit`, `channel`\* | `GET /channels/{key}/messages` | a page of a channel, oldest first (newest top-level by default; after: follow it) |
| `thread` | `read` | `id`\* | `GET /messages/{message_id}/thread` | a thread: its first message then every reply |
| `upload_file` | `write` | `filename`\*, `content_base64`\*, `content_type`, `channel`\* | `POST /channels/{key}/files/base64` | upload a file (base64) to a channel, then send it: post with its id in file_ids |
| `discard_file` | `write` | `id`\* | `DELETE /message-files/{file_id}` | take back an upload you have not sent |
| `post` | `write` | `body_md`, `parent_id`, `file_ids`, `channel`\* | `POST /channels/{key}/messages` | post to a channel, or reply in a thread with parent_id; file_ids sends your uploads |
| `edit` | `write` | `body_md`\*, `id`\* | `PATCH /messages/{message_id}` | edit your own message |
| `delete` | `write` | `id`\* | `DELETE /messages/{message_id}` | delete your own message (its thread stays) |
| `react` | `write` | `emoji`\*, `id`\* | `POST /messages/{message_id}/reactions` | add your emoji reaction to a message |
| `unreact` | `write` | `emoji`\*, `id`\* | `DELETE /messages/{message_id}/reactions/{emoji}` | remove your emoji reaction |
| `task` | `write` | `list_id`, `title`, `due_at`, `priority`, `status`, `assignees`, `tags`, `id`\* | `POST /messages/{message_id}/task` | turn a message into one task (in the channel's list unless list_id) |
| `read` | `write` | `through`, `message_ids`, `channel`\* | `POST /channels/{key}/read` | mark a channel read up to through (default its newest message) |
| `read_all` | `write` | — | `POST /channels/read-all` | mark every channel read |

## `slate_checklist`

Checklists are small ticked to-dos inside one item, not subtasks. Use them for steps of a single piece of work; tick entries as you finish them.

| Action | Scope | Params | REST | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `list` | `read` | `id`\* | `GET /items/{item_id}/checklists` | the item's checklists with their entries |
| `create` | `write` | `name`, `items`, `item_id`\* | `POST /items/{item_id}/checklists` | a checklist on item_id, optionally with its first entries |
| `rename` | `write` | `name`, `position`, `id`\* | `PATCH /checklists/{checklist_id}` | rename a checklist (position reorders it) |
| `delete` | `write` | `id`\* | `DELETE /checklists/{checklist_id}` | remove a checklist and its entries |
| `add_entry` | `write` | `title`\*, `assignee`, `position`, `checklist_id`\* | `POST /checklists/{checklist_id}/items` | add an entry to checklist_id |
| `update_entry` | `write` | `title`, `done`, `assignee`, `position`, `entry_id`\* | `PATCH /checklist-items/{entry_id}` | tick (done true), untick, rename, assign or reorder an entry |
| `remove_entry` | `write` | `entry_id`\* | `DELETE /checklist-items/{entry_id}` | delete an entry |

## `slate_view`

A view is a saved lens: layout (board, list, table, calendar, timeline or box; calendar_span month|week, timeline_zoom day|week|month), group_by (due, status, priority, assignee, tag, list, section, status_kind), sort, and a filter of {op, rules} where each rule is {field, cmp, value} or a nested group. Use it to build or adjust the lenses people look at. Example config: {layout: board, group_by: due, due_window_days: 6, sort: [{field: priority, dir: desc}, {field: due, dir: asc}], filter: {op: and, rules: [{field: status_kind, cmp: is, value: [open, active]}]}}.

| Action | Scope | Params | REST | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `list` | `read` | `scope`, `include_archived` | `GET /views` | saved views, optionally for one scope |
| `get` | `read` | `id`\* | `GET /views/{view_id}` | one saved view |
| `create` | `write` | `name`\*, `scope_kind`\*, `scope_id`, `config`\*, `position`, `shared` | `POST /views` | save a view. config example: {layout: board, group_by: due, due_window_days: 6, sort: [{field: priority, dir: desc}], filter: {op: and, rules: [{field: tag, cmp: any, value: [home]}]}, show_closed: false} |
| `update` | `write` | `name`, `config`, `position`, `shared`, `id`\* | `PATCH /views/{view_id}` | rename, reconfigure, reorder or share a view |
| `archive` | `write` | `id`\* | `POST /views/{view_id}/archive` | hide a view |
| `unarchive` | `write` | `id`\* | `POST /views/{view_id}/unarchive` | bring an archived view back |

## `slate_favorite`

Favorites are your own pinned lists, sections, saved views and items, shown as one-click chips across the top of the board. Use it to pin what you (or the account whose token you hold) will open often, or to reorder the bar.

| Action | Scope | Params | REST | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `list` | `read` | — | `GET /favorites` | your favorites in bar order, each with its target's name and scope |
| `add` | `write` | `kind`\*, `target_id`\*, `position` | `POST /favorites` | pin a list, section, saved view or item (kind + target_id); pinning twice is a no-op |
| `remove` | `write` | `id`\* | `DELETE /favorites/{favorite_id}` | unpin by favorite id |
| `reorder` | `write` | `ids`\* | `PUT /favorites/order` | set the bar order; ids must list every favorite once |

## `slate_automation`

Automations are when-this-then-that rules on a list, section or everywhere: a trigger (status changes, assignee added, due date passes...), optional conditions and actions (set status, assign, tag, comment, move, call a webhook). Use it to set up routine handling once instead of doing it by hand; read catalog first.

| Action | Scope | Params | REST | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `catalog` | `read` | — | `GET /automations/catalog` | every trigger, condition field and action with its parameters |
| `list` | `read` | `list_id`, `section_id` | `GET /automations` | rules, each with a plain-English description and its last run |
| `get` | `read` | `id`\* | `GET /automations/{automation_id}` | one rule |
| `create` | `write` | `name`\*, `list_id`, `section_id`, `trigger`\*, `conditions`, `actions`\*, `enabled` | `POST /automations` | name, trigger {type,...}, actions [{type,...}], optional conditions and list_id or section_id (neither = every list); see catalog |
| `update` | `write` | `name`, `list_id`, `section_id`, `trigger`, `conditions`, `actions`, `enabled`, `id`\* | `PATCH /automations/{automation_id}` | change any field; enabled false pauses the rule |
| `delete` | `write` | `id`\* | `DELETE /automations/{automation_id}` | remove a rule and its run log (its history stays) |
| `run` | `write` | `item_id`\*, `id`\* | `POST /automations/{automation_id}/run` | run a rule's actions on one item now (trigger and conditions skipped) |
| `rotate_secret` | `write` | `id`\* | `POST /automations/{automation_id}/secret` | a new secret for verifying the rule's webhook signatures (shown once) |
| `runs` | `read` | `id`, `limit` | `GET /automation-runs` | the run log, newest first: what fired, on which item, how each action went |

## `slate_workload`

Who has how much on: the Box view's per-person and per-agent counts (open, in progress, overdue, recently done) and open minutes against this week's capacity. Use boxes before handing work to someone, and set_capacity to say how much you can take on.

| Action | Scope | Params | REST | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `boxes` | `read` | `kinds`, `section_id`, `list_id`, `done_days` | `GET /workload/boxes` | the Box view: per person and agent (and unassigned) open, in progress, overdue and recently done counts, with open minutes against this week's capacity |
| `capacities` | `read` | `kinds` | `GET /capacities` | every person's and agent's capacity (hours a day, tasks a day, days) |
| `capacity` | `read` | `account_id`\* | `GET /accounts/{account_id}/capacity` | one account's capacity |
| `set_capacity` | `write` | `hours_per_day`, `tasks_per_day`, `work_days`, `account_id`\* | `PATCH /accounts/{account_id}/capacity` | set your own capacity (or anyone's as an admin): hours_per_day, tasks_per_day (null = no limit) and work_days (0 = Monday) |
| `reset_capacity` | `write` | `account_id`\* | `DELETE /accounts/{account_id}/capacity` | put an account's capacity back to the defaults for its kind |

## `slate_reminder`

Reminders tell an account about an item at a time, or a set time before its due date, through its inbox, check-in and phone and desktop notifications. Use it to follow up on something later; digest shows today's overdue and due work.

| Action | Scope | Params | REST | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `add` | `write` | `at`, `before_minutes`, `account`, `note`, `item_id`\* | `POST /items/{item_id}/reminders` | remind you (or `account`) about an item `at` a time, or `before_minutes` before its due date; it arrives in the inbox, check-in and on phone and desktop. Alerts before due: one call per lead (5, 15, 30, 60, 120, 1440, 2880, 10080...), any number per item; the same lead twice is one alert. Setting one for a person from a chat app: pass `account` (`alex`), else it reminds you |
| `list` | `read` | `item_id`\* | `GET /items/{item_id}/reminders` | an item's reminders, fired or not |
| `upcoming` | `read` | `limit` | `GET /reminders` | your reminders that have not gone off yet, soonest first |
| `remove` | `write` | `id`\* | `DELETE /reminders/{reminder_id}` | remove a reminder (yours, or one you set) |
| `digest` | `read` | — | `GET /me/digest` | what your daily digest says right now: overdue, due today, waiting on you |

## `slate_inbox`

Your notifications as the board's Inbox shows them: who mentioned you, what you were assigned, and what changed on items you follow, with read state. Mark what you handled as read. To poll for work on a cursor, slate_checkin is quicker.

| Action | Scope | Params | REST | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `list` | `read` | `limit`, `unread`, `reason` | `GET /inbox` | your notifications, newest first: mentions, assignments, due nudges and changes on items you are assigned to or watch |
| `count` | `read` | — | `GET /inbox/count` | how many are unread |
| `read` | `write` | `event_ids`, `item_id`, `all` | `POST /inbox/read` | mark entries read: event_ids, every entry for an item_id, or all |
| `clear` | `write` | `event_ids`, `item_id`, `all` | `POST /inbox/clear` | clear entries out of the inbox (same targets as read) |

## `slate_list`

Lists live in a section and own their statuses, which are the board's columns. Use it to find a list_id before filing items, or to create, rename or re-column a list.

| Action | Scope | Params | REST | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `list` | `read` | `section_id`, `include_archived` | `GET /lists` | lists with their statuses |
| `create` | `write` | `section_id`\*, `name`\*, `position`, `statuses`, `kind` | `POST /lists` | a list in a section (default statuses open, active, done) |
| `update` | `write` | `name`, `kind`, `section_id`, `position`, `default_status`, `archived`, `private`, `id`\* | `PATCH /lists/{list_id}` | rename, reorder, set default_status, or archived true/false |
| `set_statuses` | `write` | `statuses`\*, `fallback`, `id`\* | `PUT /lists/{list_id}/statuses` | replace the statuses (columns) in order; fallback for stranded items |

## `slate_section`

Sections are the top-level separations (for example Personal and Work). Use it to find a section, or to create or rename one when someone asks for a new audience or rhythm.

| Action | Scope | Params | REST | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `list` | `read` | `include_archived` | `GET /sections` | all sections |
| `create` | `write` | `name`\*, `audience`\*, `position` | `POST /sections` | a section (one per audience or rhythm, never per topic) |
| `update` | `write` | `whiteboard_url`, `name`, `position`, `audience`, `archived`, `private`, `id`\* | `PATCH /sections/{section_id}` | rename, reorder, change audience, or archived true/false |

## `slate_tag`

Tags cut across every section and list. Use it to see the existing tags before inventing one, or to create, rename, recolor, merge or delete a tag.

| Action | Scope | Params | REST | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `list` | `read` | — | `GET /tags` | all tags with item_count |
| `create` | `write` | `name`\*, `color` | `POST /tags` | a tag (stored lowercase) |
| `rename` | `write` | `name`, `color`, `tag`\* | `PATCH /tags/{tag}` | rename or recolor a tag; items keep it |
| `merge` | `write` | `into`\*, `tag`\* | `POST /tags/{tag}/merge` | fold a tag into another: items and rules carry `into` instead; the tag is deleted |
| `delete` | `write` | `tag`\* | `DELETE /tags/{tag}` | remove a tag from every item and rule, then delete it |

## `slate_recurrence`

Recurring rules spawn an item on a schedule (RFC 5545 RRULE, workspace timezone), or with trigger on_done the next one when the current one is done (reopen: true reuses the same task). skip_weekends moves weekend dates to Monday. Use it instead of filing dated copies of a chore by hand.

| Action | Scope | Params | REST | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `preview` | `read` | `rrule`\*, `dtstart`, `timezone`, `count`, `trigger`, `skip_weekends` | `GET /recurrences/preview` | try an RRULE without saving: next dates and the rule in plain English |
| `upcoming` | `read` | `start`\*, `end`\*, `list_id` | `GET /recurrences/upcoming` | dates scheduled rules will fill in a window that are not items yet |
| `list` | `read` | `list_id`, `include_ended` | `GET /recurrences` | recurrence rules, optionally in one list |
| `get` | `read` | `id`\* | `GET /recurrences/{rule_id}` | one rule with its next occurrences |
| `create` | `write` | `body_template_md`, `priority`, `tags`, `assignees`, `dtstart`, `timezone`, `lead_days`, `missed_policy`, `trigger`, `skip_weekends`, `reopen`, `copy_checklists`, `list_id`\*, `title_template`\*, `rrule`\*, `adopt_item_id` | `POST /recurrences` | a rule that spawns one item per occurrence |
| `update` | `write` | `body_template_md`, `priority`, `tags`, `assignees`, `dtstart`, `timezone`, `lead_days`, `missed_policy`, `trigger`, `skip_weekends`, `reopen`, `copy_checklists`, `list_id`, `title_template`, `rrule`, `ended`, `id`\* | `PATCH /recurrences/{rule_id}` | change a rule (`ended: true` ends it for good) |
| `pause` | `write` | `id`\* | `POST /recurrences/{rule_id}/pause` | stop spawning |
| `resume` | `write` | `id`\* | `POST /recurrences/{rule_id}/resume` | start spawning again from today |
| `adopt` | `write` | `item_id`\*, `id`\* | `POST /recurrences/{rule_id}/adopt` | make an existing item the rule's current occurrence (it keeps its due date) |
| `run_now` | `write` | `id`\* | `POST /recurrences/{rule_id}/run-now` | spawn everything due within the rule's lead window now |

## `slate_webhook`

Webhooks POST signed events to your URL so you are woken instead of polling. Use it to register, inspect or test your own doorbell.

| Action | Scope | Params | REST | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `list` | `write` | — | `GET /webhooks` | your webhooks (an admin sees everyone's) |
| `create` | `write` | `url`\*, `events`\*, `filter` | `POST /webhooks` | subscribe a URL to event types; the reply holds the signing secret, shown only once |
| `update` | `write` | `url`, `events`, `filter`, `disabled`, `id`\* | `PATCH /webhooks/{webhook_id}` | change url, events, filter (replaced whole) or disabled |
| `deliveries` | `write` | `limit`, `offset`, `id`\* | `GET /webhooks/{webhook_id}/deliveries` | the delivery log, newest first |
| `test` | `write` | `id`\* | `POST /webhooks/{webhook_id}/test` | send a webhook.test delivery now (one attempt) and return its outcome |

## `slate_account`

Accounts are the people and agents who own and change items; assignees are account handles. Use `me` to learn who you are; the other actions need an admin token.

| Action | Scope | Params | REST | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `me` | `read` | — | `GET /me` | who this token is, and its scopes |
| `list` | `admin` | — | `GET /accounts` | all accounts (admin) |
| `create` | `admin` | `handle`\*, `display_name`\*, `kind`\*, `role`, `wake` | `POST /accounts` | a person or agent account (admin) |
| `create_token` | `admin` | `scopes`\*, `label`, `limit`, `account_id`\* | `POST /accounts/{account_id}/tokens` | issue a token; its plaintext is shown only in this result (admin) |
| `update` | `admin` | `display_name`, `disabled`, `wake`, `account_id`\* | `PATCH /accounts/{account_id}` | rename an account, or disable it (`disabled: true` stops its tokens at once) (admin) |
| `tokens` | `read` | `include_revoked`, `account_id`\* | `GET /accounts/{account_id}/tokens` | an account's tokens with last use, never the secret (admin, or your own) |
| `usage` | `read` | `days`, `account_id`\* | `GET /accounts/{account_id}/usage` | events per day by source, busiest event types, requests per token (admin, or yours) |
| `revoke_token` | `read` | `token_id`\* | `DELETE /tokens/{token_id}` | revoke a token at once (admin, or your own token) |
| `set_role` | `admin` | `role`\*, `account_id`\* | `PUT /accounts/{account_id}/role` | change an account's role: owner, admin, member, guest (admin; admins only by the owner) |
| `access` | `read` | `account_id`\* | `GET /accounts/{account_id}/access` | every section and list an account reaches, with its level (admin, or yourself) |
| `agent_rules` | `admin` | — | `GET /settings/agents` | what agent accounts may never do here, whatever their token (admin) |
| `set_agent_rules` | `admin` | `denied`\* | `PUT /settings/agents` | replace what agents may never do: `denied` lists action keys (owner or admin person) |

## `slate_today`

Your day across every section: overdue, due before midnight workspace time, and items waiting on you, most urgent first. Use it to decide what to work on next.

| Action | Scope | Params | REST | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `get` | `read` | `fields` | `GET /today` | overdue, due today, waiting on you (`fields` trims each item) |

## `slate_checkin`

Start here each time you wake: `queue` is your open items (assigned to you or waiting on you), most urgent first; `news` is what other accounts did that concerns you since your last call (assigned, unassigned, mentioned, reply, waiting_on_you, on_your_item, watching, reminder, digest); a chat mention or thread reply carries the message in `after` (answer with slate_chat). Keep `next_since` and pass it back as `since`.

| Action | Scope | Params | REST | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `get` | `read` | `since`, `limit`, `queue_limit`, `fields`, `wait` | `GET /checkin` | your open items (queue) and others' events that concern you (news, with why), from a cursor |

## `slate_work`

The agent work loop in three calls: `next` takes your best free task (with a lease so nobody else takes it), `heartbeat` keeps it while you work, `finish` reports back (outcome, comment, hand-off) and can take the next one. Use it instead of picking tasks from slate_checkin by hand.

| Action | Scope | Params | REST | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `reconcile` | `write` | `run_id`\*, `state`\*, `evidence`\*, `item_id`\* | `POST /work/{item_id}/reconcile` | confirm remote termination with run proof and actual runtime evidence; unlock without completing |
| `chat_heartbeat` | `write` | `run_id`, `channel`\*, `thread_id`, `lease_seconds` | `POST /work/chat/heartbeat` | renew a chat turn with its run_id proof |
| `chat_finish` | `write` | `run_id`, `channel`\*, `thread_id`, `outcome`\*, `reply`, `note` | `POST /work/chat/finish` | settle only the proved chat attempt; identical retries return its durable receipt |
| `chat_reconcile` | `write` | `run_id`\*, `state`\*, `evidence`\*, `channel`\*, `thread_id` | `POST /work/chat/reconcile` | confirm remote chat termination with run proof and actual runtime evidence |
| `doc_heartbeat` | `write` | `run_id`, `doc_id`\*, `thread_id`, `lease_seconds` | `POST /work/doc/heartbeat` | renew a doc turn (a page mention from next) with its run_id proof |
| `doc_finish` | `write` | `run_id`, `doc_id`\*, `thread_id`, `outcome`\*, `reply`, `note` | `POST /work/doc/finish` | end a doc turn: done with reply posts your comment in the thread (a new discussion thread for a mention in the page body); release posts nothing. Identical retries return its durable receipt |
| `doc_reconcile` | `write` | `run_id`\*, `state`\*, `evidence`\*, `doc_id`\*, `thread_id` | `POST /work/doc/reconcile` | confirm remote doc-turn termination with run proof and actual runtime evidence |
| `next` | `write` | `kinds`, `run_id`, `lease_seconds`, `pool`, `list_id`, `section_id`, `tag`, `item_id`, `channel`, `thread_id`, `doc_id`, `resume`, `note`, `context`, `wait` | `POST /work/next` | take your next task: the best open one assigned to you or waiting on you (pool: also unassigned ones) that is not blocked, not held by another agent and not waiting on a person; priority order, then due date. It is yours for lease_seconds; item is null when none is free (wait: long-poll for one) |
| `heartbeat` | `write` | `run_id`, `lease_seconds`, `note`, `progress`, `url`, `thread`, `item_id`\* | `POST /work/{item_id}/heartbeat` | keep holding the task (the lease runs lease_seconds from now); note/progress update the badge. An error saying you do not hold it means stop: another agent has it |
| `finish` | `write` | `run_id`, `outcome`\*, `note`, `comment`, `progress`, `status`, `hand_to`, `waiting_on`, `url`, `reply`, `thread`, `next`, `item_id`\* | `POST /work/{item_id}/finish` | report back in one call: outcome done / review / later (stay assigned, no badge, the due time still to come runs you again) / blocked (waiting_on) / release, a note posted as your comment, a status, hand_to another account; next: {} also takes your next task. Agent finishes consume only taken Ask dispatches, not resolution; asked-only agent done explicitly resolves only its taken Asks. New/reassigned Asks during the run remain pending; humans must explicitly resolve |
| `held` | `read` | — | `GET /work` | the tasks you hold now and when each lease runs out |
| `plan` | `read` | — | `GET /agents/plan` | what each agent is about to run in the next 24 h, by the same rule as `next`: tasks whose run time comes (reason due), Run now presses (run_requested), open Asks (ask), and the tasks each holds now with their age; soonest first |

## `slate_doc`

Docs are nested Markdown pages (plans, notes, specs, logs) in a list, a section or the workspace, with page history; [[task:<id>]] embeds a live task card. Use it to keep a plan or work log, read what people wrote, or file tasks from a page. A page that starts with a ```facts block of `key: value` lines (a policy number, a renewal date) is a record: `get` returns them as `facts` and search finds a value; write or change them with `update` like any body text.

| Action | Scope | Params | REST | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `list` | `read` | `q`, `list_id`, `section_id`, `parent_id`, `workspace`, `archived`, `embeds`, `limit`, `kind`, `tag` | `GET /docs` | pages in tree order without bodies; q searches titles and bodies |
| `get` | `read` | `id`\* | `GET /docs/{doc_id}` | one page: body, path, subpages, outline, embedded tasks, links, backlinks, files |
| `templates` | `read` | — | `GET /docs/templates` | starting points for create's template |
| `create` | `write` | `title`, `body_md`, `icon`, `parent_id`, `list_id`, `section_id`, `template`, `before_id`, `kind`, `tags` | `POST /docs` | a page in list_id, section_id, the workspace (neither) or under parent_id; body_md is Markdown, [[task:<id>]] embeds a task card, [[doc:<id>]] links a page |
| `update` | `write` | `title`, `icon`, `body_md`, `append_md`, `replace_section`, `base_revision`, `new_version`, `note`, `tags`, `id`\* | `PATCH /docs/{doc_id}` | edit title, icon or body: body_md replaces, append_md adds at the end, replace_section {heading, body_md} rewrites one part; base_revision guards against overwriting a newer edit; note names a page-history version |
| `move` | `write` | `parent_id`, `list_id`, `section_id`, `before_id`, `id`\* | `POST /docs/{doc_id}/move` | move under parent_id, or to the top of list_id / section_id / the workspace; before_id orders it |
| `archive` | `write` | `id`\* | `POST /docs/{doc_id}/archive` | hide a page and its subpages |
| `unarchive` | `write` | `id`\* | `POST /docs/{doc_id}/unarchive` | bring an archived page back |
| `delete` | `write` | `id`\* | `DELETE /docs/{doc_id}` | delete an archived page and its subpages for good |
| `duplicate` | `write` | `title`, `subpages`, `id`\* | `POST /docs/{doc_id}/duplicate` | copy a page (and its subpages) next to it |
| `versions` | `read` | `id`\* | `GET /docs/{doc_id}/versions` | page history, newest first (no bodies) |
| `version` | `read` | `id`\*, `version_no`\* | `GET /docs/{doc_id}/versions/{version_no}` | one version with its body |
| `diff` | `read` | `from_version`\*, `to_version`, `id`\* | `GET /docs/{doc_id}/diff` | unified diff of the body between two versions (default to: the current text) |
| `restore` | `write` | `id`\*, `version_no`\* | `POST /docs/{doc_id}/versions/{version_no}/restore` | put an older version's title and body back (as a new version) |
| `create_task` | `write` | `body_md`, `body_note`, `status`, `priority`, `start_at`, `due_at`, `waiting_on_account_id`, `acceptance_md`, `position`, `kind`, `external_ref`, `assignees`, `tags`, `estimate_minutes`, `title`\*, `list_id`, `replace`, `occurrence`, `base_revision`, `id`\* | `POST /docs/{doc_id}/tasks` | file one task from the page: replace names the text that becomes its live card (else the card is added at the end); the task links back. Slate rule: create makes exactly one item; use split for subtasks. |
| `attach` | `write` | `filename`\*, `content_base64`\*, `content_type`, `id`\* | `POST /docs/{doc_id}/files/base64` | upload an image or file into the page; paste the returned markdown into the body |
| `remove_file` | `write` | `file_id`\* | `DELETE /doc-files/{file_id}` | remove an uploaded file |
| `upload` | `write` | `filename`\*, `content_base64`\*, `content_type`, `note`\*, `id`\* | `POST /docs/{doc_id}/revisions/base64` | the next revision of a file doc (a PDF, spreadsheet, photo); the previous revision stays, superseded; note says what changed and is required |
| `revisions` | `read` | `id`\* | `GET /docs/{doc_id}/revisions` | a file doc's revisions, newest first (metadata; bytes at each url) |
| `restore_revision` | `write` | `id`\*, `revision_no`\* | `POST /docs/{doc_id}/revisions/{revision_no}/restore` | make an older revision of a file doc current again (as a new revision) |
| `hub` | `read` | `section_id`\* | `GET /sections/{section_id}/documents` | a section's documents hub: its drawers with counts, pages outside any drawer, what needs you (open asks to you, open review threads by others on docs you touched) |
| `drawer` | `read` | `folder`, `list_id`\* | `GET /lists/{list_id}/drawer` | a drawer's entries (folders and documents) at its top or inside a folder, with revisions, pins, tags, thread counts; a drawer is a list of kind drawer |
| `to_drawer` | `write` | `id`\* | `POST /docs/{doc_id}/to-drawer` | turn a top-level page into a drawer of the same name in its section (its subpages become the entries; the page moves in too) |
| `pin_revision` | `write` | `note`, `id`\*, `revision_no`\* | `POST /docs/{doc_id}/revisions/{revision_no}/pin` | mark a file doc's revision as the one in use; one pin per doc |
| `unpin_revision` | `write` | `id`\* | `DELETE /docs/{doc_id}/pin` | take the pin off a file doc |
| `pin_to_top` | `write` | `id`\* | `POST /docs/{doc_id}/top` | pin a document (file, page or folder) to the top of its drawer or folder listing, for everyone |
| `unpin_from_top` | `write` | `id`\* | `DELETE /docs/{doc_id}/top` | take a document off the top of its drawer or folder listing |
| `compare_revisions` | `read` | `id`\*, `from_revision`\*, `to_revision` | `GET /docs/{doc_id}/revisions/compare` | what changed between two revisions of a file doc: text files line by line, CSV/XLSX cell by cell per sheet, PDFs by extracted text (approximate); images none |
| `comments` | `read` | `id`\* | `GET /docs/{doc_id}/comments` | every comment on the doc, oldest first (review threads carry an anchor and can be resolved; discussion has none; replies carry parent_id) |
| `comment` | `write` | `body_md`\*, `parent_id`, `viewed_revision`, `anchor`, `suggestion_md`, `assignee`, `id`\* | `POST /docs/{doc_id}/comments` | comment on a page or file: with anchor (quote/start/end on a page; page and/or x,y on a file) a review thread, without one discussion; parent_id replies; suggestion_md proposes replacement text for the quote; assignee makes it an Ask |
| `edit_comment` | `write` | `body_md`\*, `comment_id`\* | `PATCH /doc-comments/{comment_id}` | edit your own doc comment |
| `resolve_comment` | `write` | `comment_id`\* | `POST /doc-comments/{comment_id}/resolve` | close a review thread or Ask (its first comment) |
| `reopen_comment` | `write` | `comment_id`\* | `POST /doc-comments/{comment_id}/reopen` | reopen a resolved thread |
| `assign_comment` | `write` | `assignee`, `comment_id`\* | `POST /doc-comments/{comment_id}/assign` | address a doc comment to an account (an Ask), or take it off |
| `accept_suggestion` | `write` | `comment_id`\* | `POST /doc-comments/{comment_id}/accept` | apply a review comment's suggestion_md to the page and resolve the thread |
| `activity` | `read` | `limit`, `id`\* | `GET /docs/{doc_id}/activity` | the doc's comments plus the events the side panel folds in (revisions, saves, moves, resolved threads), oldest first |

## `slate_agents`

The roster of agent accounts: who is online, what each is working on (their current reports), how many open items each holds. Use it before picking up work, to see whether another agent is already on it.

| Action | Scope | Params | REST | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `list` | `read` | `kind` | `GET /agents` | each agent's presence (online, last_seen_at), current reports (working), open assignments and events in the last 24 h |

## `slate_health`

Whether Slate is working: background pollers, engines, error rates and slow calls per token, failed automations and queue depths (owners and admins). Use it when calls fail or seem slow, before reporting Slate as broken.

| Action | Scope | Params | REST | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `get` | `read` | — | `GET /health` | Slate's health (owners and admins): overall status and checks, background pollers (last run, last success, errors), engines, calls and errors per token in the last hour, latency percentiles, failed automation runs, queues, database size |

## `slate_batch`

Run up to 100 calls of the other tools in one round trip, all-or-nothing by default (atomic: false commits each op alone). Use it to file or change many things at once; a string param `$ref.field` reuses an earlier op's result.

| Action | Scope | Params | REST | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `run` | `read` | `ops`\*, `atomic`, `views` | `POST /batch` | {atomic, results: [{ok, result | error}]}, one slot per op in order |

## `slate_events`

Every change on Slate is an event with an actor. Use it to catch up on everything that changed, or audit one account (actor); keep next_since and pass it back as since. For only what concerns you, slate_checkin is the filtered version.

| Action | Scope | Params | REST | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `poll` | `read` | `since`, `type`, `item_id`, `actor`, `actor_kind`, `tail`, `limit` | `GET /events` | events after `since`, oldest first; pass next_since back |

## `slate_share`

Who can see and change what: share a section or list with a person or agent at view, comment or edit, make one private, and see who reaches it. Owner and admin only; roles are slate_account set_role.

| Action | Scope | Params | REST | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `list` | `admin` | `account_id`, `scope_kind`, `scope_id` | `GET /shares` | shares, by account and/or section/list (admin) |
| `set` | `admin` | `account_id`\*, `scope_kind`\*, `scope_id`\*, `level`\* | `PUT /shares` | share a section or list with an account at view, comment or edit; level null revokes (admin) |
| `who` | `admin` | `scope_kind`\*, `scope_id`\* | `GET /lists/{list_id}/access` | everyone who reaches a section or list, at what level and why (admin) |
| `private` | `write` | `scope_kind`\*, `scope_id`\*, `private`\* | `PATCH /lists/{list_id}` | make a section or list private (members stop seeing it unless shared) or public (admin) |

## `slate_audit`

The audit log: every change with who did it (person or agent), when, through which door (ui, api, mcp, system) and on what, newest first. Use it to answer who changed this, or what an agent did today; it only shows what your access can read.

| Action | Scope | Params | REST | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `list` | `read` | `actor`, `actor_kind`, `source`, `type`, `item_id`, `list_id`, `section_id`, `since`, `until`, `q`, `before`, `limit` | `GET /audit` | who (person or agent) did what, when, through which door; newest first, filterable; pass next_before back as before |
| `facets` | `read` | — | `GET /audit/facets` | event types and actors in the log you can see |

## `slate_export`

Take Slate's data out: a list, a section or everything as one JSON document with every task, comment, checklist and link. Use it for a report, an archive or a move; empty_trash (admins) clears the trash for good.

| Action | Scope | Params | REST | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `json` | `read` | `list_id`, `section_id`, `include_archived` | `GET /export` | a list, a section or everything as one JSON document: every task (the item shape) with comments, checklists and links, plus the lists, statuses, tags and fields around them; trashed tasks are left out |
| `empty_trash` | `admin` | — | `POST /trash/empty` | delete everything in the trash for good (admins) |

## `slate_search`

One search over everything on Slate: tasks (title and description), docs (title, page text and the text inside files) and chat messages, as typed hits. Use it when you are looking for something and do not know whether it is a task, a page or a message.

| Action | Scope | Params | REST | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `search` | `read` | `q`\*, `limit` | `GET /search` | find q in tasks (title, description), docs (title, page text, file text) and chat messages at once: typed hits, tasks first, then docs, then messages (newest first); only what you can read; `%` and `_` are literal |
